reason: None of the cited evidence addresses Mg-containing lightweight HEAs, cooling-rate effects on phase transformation, or the link between intermetallics and protective oxide formation. E1–E3 discuss corrosion of a NiFeCoAl MEA in different solutions, E4 describes transformative HEAs and friction stir processing, and E5 outlines CALPHAD optimization and induction melting of Al-based alloys without testing the proposed mechanism.
premises: Slower cooling transforms metastable Mg-rich solid solution into stable intermetallic compounds
These intermetallics serve as nucleation sites for protective oxide scale formation
The resulting oxide scale reduces corrosion and high-temperature oxidation rates
Rapid cooling retains a higher fraction of metastable phases lacking such heterogeneities
The mechanism applies to Mg-containing lightweight HEAs analogous to Al–MgCuZnGd
